newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Riksbank cuts key repo rate to 4.35 pct.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Riksbank cuts key repo rate to 4.35 pct.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, on Tuesday cut its key interest rate, the repo rate, by 25 basis points to 4.35 percent.
The Riksbank said the 23rd cut this year to the repo rate, the bank's key tool for controlling money market liquidity, was permissible because inflation is in line with its targets.
"The Riksbank judges that the outlook for inflation continues to be in line with the inflation target," the bank said in a statement.
The bank said that for administrative reasons as well as because of the Christmas and New Year holiday, the repo which will be announced on December 17 will run for three weeks.

Ahead of the repo announcement, analysts were mixed on whether the Riksbank would again lower the repo that began the year at 8.91 percent or wait until after its next inflation report for the year is released on December 17.

The new seven-day reverse repurchase operation will run from November 27 to December 4. All primary dealers must submit bids to the Riksbank by 0900 GMT on November 26. Seven out of 16 analysts forecast the repo would be lowered while the rest expected the bank to wait.

The repo rate is the central in the Riksbank's three tier rate system. The deposit and lending rates, which mark the floor and ceiling of the interest rate corridor, currently stand at 4.25 percent and 5.75 percent.
